methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort (n=363) with a clinically homogeneous population (metastatic NSCLC, PD-L1 TPS >=50%, no actionable driver, first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy). Strengths: uniform management protocol, protocolized thyroid monitoring every 6 weeks, exclusion of baseline thyroid disease, CTCAE v5 grading, Cox regression with irTD as time-varying covariate, and landmark analyses at 3 and 6 months to mitigate immortal-time bias. Limitations candidly acknowledged: no corticosteroid/autoimmune history, no thyroid autoantibodies, OS data immature, single-center design, 6-weekly testing may miss transient thyrotoxic phases. Multivariable modeling followed standard practice but no sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounders.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single retrospective cohort study maps to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical relevance is direct and timely: irTD is proposed as an easily measured, inexpensive on-treatment biomarker of immune activation in a group where ~50% fail to derive durable benefit from pembrolizumab. The PFS difference is striking (26.3 vs 6.2 months) and remains significant after landmark adjustment. Findings have immediate implications for patient monitoring and hypothesis generation for prospective biomarker studies, though OS data remain immature.

reporting_quality.justification: As an observational cohort study, STROBE is applicable. Most STROBE items are addressed: study design and setting, eligibility criteria, variable definitions (irTD, early/late per SITC), data sources, statistical methods (Cox time-varying covariate, landmark analyses), participant flow (with table breakdowns), and transparent discussion of limitations. Adverse events graded per CTCAE v5, thyroid dysfunction defined per standard biochemical thresholds, and SITC consensus used for timing classification. No missing data handling described in detail. Data availability is limited (clinical registry with anonymized extraction), and no code is shared.

novelty_literature.justification: Association of irTD with improved PFS in NSCLC ICI therapy has been reported in multiple prior cohorts (Chilelli, Cai, Thuillier, D'Aiello, Ceric, Wu cited), and this study is explicitly positioned as reinforcement of existing evidence. Distinctive elements: uniform PD-L1 TPS>=50% first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy cohort with relatively large N, rigorous time-varying/landmark adjustment, and exploration of early-vs-late onset timing. Not first-in-class but a meaningful extension with rigorous ITB handling.

writing_presentation.justification: Clearly written and well-organized with precise clinical vocabulary. Methods, results, and discussion flow logically. Tables and figures are appropriately referenced. Limitations are thoroughly discussed with appropriate humility. Minor issues: one sentence about ethics committee approval date (4 December 2025) appears to post-date patient enrollment (2021-2024), which may be an error or indicate an amendment; some redundancy across introduction paragraphs. Overall publication-quality prose.

key_strengths: Large (n=363), clinically homogeneous real-world cohort (PD-L1 TPS>=50%, non-oncogene-addicted, first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy) reducing therapeutic heterogeneity
Rigorous statistical handling of immortal-time bias via time-varying Cox and 3/6-month landmark analyses
Protocolized 6-weekly thyroid function testing at baseline and during treatment improves case ascertainment
Large effect size (HR 0.378 for PFS) persists after landmark adjustment, strengthening causal plausibility
Transparent limitations including immature OS, lack of autoantibody testing, and single-center design
key_concerns: Retrospective, single-center design limits generalizability beyond the Serbian reimbursement context
OS data immature; PFS alone insufficient to confirm durable benefit as predictive biomarker
Thyroid autoantibodies and corticosteroid/autoimmune history not captured, limiting mechanistic inference
Ethics approval date (December 2025) appears inconsistent with enrollment window (2021-2024) and needs clarification
Incremental novelty over published similar associations in NSCLC cohorts
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid real-world biomarker study with appropriate ITB handling and a clinically meaningful signal. Fits Tier 3 with minor revisions to clarify ethics approval date and acknowledge incremental nature.
